subject: Post-call: performance gating & connection-pool path to prod
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: performance gating & connection-pool path to prod

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we put an engineering plan together.

Key points I captured from the call:
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 350ms for single-turn streaming responses, p99 <= 900ms (for the baseline model used in demo).
- Expected concurrency: 80–120 concurrent user streams at peak; each stream typically produces 8–12 tokens/sec, bursts up to ~30 tokens/sec.
- Average request size: 280 tokens (including prompt + response).
- Seq length assumptions: prompt ~120 tokens, response ~160 tokens; sometimes longer for diagnostic flows.
- Connection behavior: clients will use long-lived HTTP/2 streams and expect server-side streaming. Connection pool per client will maintain 12–20 concurrent HTTP/2 channels.
- Desired throughput: sustained ~600 requests/minute with brief bursts to 1,500 requests/minute during heavy load windows.

Open questions for you (please confirm by EOD Wednesday so we can scope infra):
1) Can you confirm the 80–120 concurrent streams number is peak or sustained? If peak, what's the typical sustained concurrency?
2) Any non-standard networking (e.g., outbound proxies, mTLS, strict NAT timeouts) that would affect long-lived streams?
3) Is TLS termination happening in your VPC (you indicated Private deployment was a possibility) or do you plan to use Redwood hosted endpoints?

Proposed Redwood path to prod (high level):
- Short PoC (1 week): we run a taped replay of your production traces against hosted Redwood with an engineered client to validate latency and connection behavior.
- Quota request: we’ll raise a temporary rate/concurrency increase for the PoC (we'll need a HubSpot ticket + signed A/N agreement).
- Longer PoC (2 weeks): run steady-state load tests with streaming enabled to validate KV/cache warmup and connection pooling effects.
- If metrics align, move to Dedicated or Private deployment with reserved capacity and a pre-warmed connection pool.

Action items I’ll take this week:
- Share a minimal PoC checklist + a sample load driver you can run locally (attaching connpool_diagram.pdf and acme_poc_requirements.xlsx).
- Open a quota increase request for concurrent streams to support the PoC (we’ll include the exact numbers once you confirm answers above).

Ask: can you reply with the answers to Q1–Q3 and attach any sample traces you have? That will let us size the connection pool and propose an exact quota number.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0173

From: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@acme.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, legal@acme.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance gating & connection-pool path to prod

Sergio — thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming the items below:

- Concurrency: the 80–120 figure is peak concurrency during business hours. Typical sustained concurrency is ~55–70 concurrent streams. We see short spike windows (2–3 minutes) where it reaches ~120.
- Networking: no special outbound proxy; clients are inside our managed fleet (GKE) — we do have aggressive NAT timeouts in one region (30s) but keepalive is enabled. We can adjust if needed.
- TLS: for initial PoC we want to use Redwood hosted endpoints (easier for security review). If the PoC looks good we will evaluate Private (VPC) deployment for production.

Two additional asks from our side:
1) We need to understand Redwood’s temporary/poC concurrency limit process and timelines. Can you list typical lead times for increases?
2) For streaming, do you recommend persistent HTTP/2 connections with multiple concurrent streams or multiple separate TCP connections? Our client library currently prefers 1–2 long-lived connections with multiple concurrent streams per connection.

I’ll attach a 48-hour sample trace (anonymized) in a follow-up note.

—Tom
Tom Jenkins
Head of Platform
Acme AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: performance gating & connection-pool path to prod

Looping infra and capacity so we can move quickly — copying relevant bits below and adding recommended next steps.

Notes / recommendations:
- PoC quota: propose temporary increase to support 150 concurrent streaming sessions for 1 week to cover spike windows (security review permitting). Historically we can provision this on hosted within 48–72 hours after HubSpot ticket + basic onboarding.
- Connection pooling: for HTTP/2 streaming we recommend persistent connections with multiple concurrent streams per connection. Client pattern of 1–2 long-lived connections with ~12 streams each aligns well with our runtime (it reduces TLS overhead and helps KV cache locality).
- Rate limiting: Redwood enforces per-project rate limits at the edge. For hosted customers we can define a per-API-key concurrency cap and per-minute token throughput. For durability, we recommend setting a soft quota (e.g., 120 concurrent, 1,000 req/min) and an emergency burst cap for testing only.

Immediate asks from infra (Karthik):
- Please file quota increase request for account ACME-12345 (temp 150 concurrent streams, 2,000 req/min) and note streaming usage. Attach the PoC checklist.
- Pre-warm the model instance pool with a lightweight warmup script using the supplied trace to validate KV cache hit rates.

I’ve attached connpool_diagram.pdf to illustrate recommended client topology. Sergio — can you confirm we should request the 150/2,000 numbers for the PoC? If so I’ll open the HubSpot ticket and tag support to fast-track.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance gating & connection-pool path to prod

Marissa — that sounds good and matches our expectations. Please proceed with the temporary PoC quota of 150 concurrent streams and 2,000 req/min. We will run the 48-hour trace against the hosted endpoint this week.

Next steps we can commit to from Acme side:
- I will share the anonymized 48-hour traces by EOD today (attaching to the HubSpot ticket once you open it).
- We’ll update our client to use 2 persistent HTTP/2 connections with up to 12 concurrent streams each (should match your recommendations).
- If the PoC validates, we expect to discuss Dedicated capacity (1–2 reserved GPU pools) and an SLA.

Please send the HubSpot ticket link and the PoC checklist + sample load driver. We’ll aim to start the PoC on Monday.

Thanks — Tom
